patterns_data.top_pattern: CO inpatient spend rose across product, PA, and facility mix
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: CO Commercial Local Group inpatient spend across PPO CHILDRENS and PPO/EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL
patterns_data.pattern_details: CO shows the largest operational pressure, but it is not coming from one simple source. PPO CHILDRENS admissions requiring PA increased, EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL cases without PA also increased, and PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL cases showed added spend even as volume fell because paid per admit rose. The business story is a combined product, PA, and facility mix issue rather than a single utilization spike.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is the largest actionable inpatient cost pattern and it touches UM, reimbursement, and product-specific hospital management at the same time.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a CO inpatient action pack by product and facility: reprice PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL unit-cost inflation, review EPO no-PA ACUTE HOSPITAL admission rules, and confirm PA policy performance for PPO CHILDRENS admissions.
evidence_summary: CO PPO CHILDRENS with PA added about $1.5M, with admissions up 7 and paid per admit up about $20.7K.
CO EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL without PA added about $1.3M, with admissions up 5 and paid per admit up about $21.0K.
CO PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL with PA added about $0.6M even as admissions fell 16, pointing to unit-cost pressure rather than volume growth.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Several inpatient increases are landing in Not Mapped facility buckets or in auth-code distribution movement rather than clean operational categories. That makes it unsafe to interpret these as pure utilization, site-of-care, or PA-performance changes until the classification is fixed. This is a gating data and coding issue before broader business action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the mapping is wrong, the organization could take the wrong UM, reimbursement, or network action against the wrong segment.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Correct facility mapping and auth-code attribution for the affected CA, CO, and NY claims, then rerun the impacted inpatient segments before changing PA policy, provider action, or pricing strategy.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The findings are explicitly flagged as unmapped or auth-code shifts and require validation before action.
evidence_summary: CO PPO Not Mapped claims added about $0.5M from 12 more admissions while paid per admit fell, suggesting volume moved into an unmapped bucket.
CA Not Mapped claims added about $0.4M in PPO and about $0.3M in HMO, heavily concentrated at UC IRVINE MEDICAL CENTER.
NY auth-code distribution movement added about $0.3M in postpartum claims with no reliable volume or unit-cost signal for business action yet.

key_driver_codes: Postpartum and Postabortion Diagnoses without O.R. Procedures
patterns_data.pattern_details: NY has a distinct maternity pattern centered on postpartum preeclampsia complications. Severe preeclampsia is primarily a volume story, while unspecified preeclampsia adds a smaller intensity component. This should be managed as an OB-specific episode pattern, not folded into general Med/Surg inpatient action.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternity complication growth needs different clinical, UM, and care-management actions than digestive or general acute hospital trends.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a focused OB review on NY postpartum preeclampsia admissions to verify severity coding, identify readmission or complication pathways, and target maternal care management interventions.
evidence_summary: Severe preeclampsia in the puerperium added about $245K from 13 more admissions with little change in paid per admit.
Unspecified preeclampsia in the puerperium added about $75K from 3 admissions, with paid per admit up about $9.3K.
